candidate.description_text: The Austrian SME, founded in 2012, develops innovative technologies for surface functionalization, with a particular focus on the metallization of technical substrates. Together with their partners, they can draw on many years of experience in plasma technology, systems engineering and production automation. A key area of application is the functionalization of aluminum surfaces to make them suitable for subsequent soldering processes, such as those used in the electronics and printed circuit board industries. This makes it possible to replace the conventionally used copper with aluminum, which is cheaper and much lighter. The Austrian company already has established market access to the electronics industry and specifically targets applications in the fields of printed circuit boards, electronic assemblies, and innovative connection technologies. As part of the further development of this technology, the SME is now seeking industrial partners with experience in etching aluminum structures, such as those typically found in printed circuit boards and electronic assemblies.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Potential partners could include, for example: •    manufacturers of chemicals for aluminum etching •    chemical processors or process service providers for aluminum etching •    equipment manufacturers with expertise in etching and inline processing Ideally, partners should come from the following fields: •    etching of formed parts, •    spray etching of fine metal structures, •    or continuous inline etching processes for metallic materials. The Austrian SME is looking for partners who: •    can provide suitable etching chemicals and process chemicals, •    possess in-depth expertise in etching processes and integration into industrial manufacturing processes, •    actively support joint technological development, •    and are interested in the subsequent joint marketing of the technology in the printed circuit board and electronics markets. Of particular importance is a process chemistry that can be implemented as simply, reliably, and cost-effectively as possible on existing etching lines in the electronics industry or on lines modified with minimal effort.

candidate.description_text: An Austrian company operating in the field of sustainable timber construction is developing next-generation building systems based on prefabricated timber panels. To further improve the environmental performance, circularity and adaptability of its construction solutions, the company is seeking an innovative connection technology for joining structural timber elements. Current fastening and connection solutions often require compromises between structural performance, ease of assembly, material health and circularity. The company is therefore looking for a novel connection concept that can simultaneously address these requirements while remaining suitable for industrial production and large-scale construction applications. The requested technology should enable the connection of timber wall, roof and floor elements in load-bearing applications. The solution should support modern industrial prefabrication processes and facilitate efficient on-site assembly, maintenance and future building modifications. The company is particularly interested in technologies that support circular construction principles through reversible and non-destructive disassembly, enabling multiple use cycles and preserving the value of building components and materials throughout their lifecycle. Potential cooperation may involve adaptation of an existing technology, co-development of a new connection system, testing and validation activities, material optimisation or industrial implementation. The company is open to commercial agreements with technical assistance as well as research and development cooperation agreements.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company seeks a future-proof connection system designed according to open-building and circular-construction principles, ensuring long-term adaptability, interoperability and material innovation readiness. The sought technology should fulfil the following functional requirements: •	Suitable for structural timber construction applications. •	Enables connections between wall, roof and floor elements. •	Capable of transferring vertical, horizontal and dynamic loads. •	High mechanical strength and long-term durability. •	Suitable for repeated assembly and disassembly cycles. •	Compatible with industrial prefabrication processes. •	Facilitates rapid installation, maintenance and replacement. •	Supports future extensions, modifications and adaptive reuse of buildings. Material-related requirements include: •	Use of recyclable materials. •	Preference for PFAS-free solutions. •	Compliance with REACH regulations. •	Absence of substances of very high concern (SVHC). •	Efficient material use with low material intensity. •	High corrosion resistance. •	Long service life. •	Possibility to integrate bio-based materials or components. •	Low-emission materials supporting indoor air quality. •	Low VOC emissions and minimisation of hazardous substances. •	Consideration of human health criteria aligned with sustainability certification systems such as DGNB, Cradle-to-Cradle and LEED. Circular economy requirements include: •	Non-destructive disassembly. •	Multiple reuse cycles without significant performance loss. •	Easy separation of materials at end-of-life. •	Support for pure material streams and high-quality recycling. •	Preservation of material value throughout the lifecycle. •	Compatibility with cradle-to-cradle design principles. •	Potential integration into take-back systems. •	Facilitation of secondary markets and remanufacturing of building components. System-level requirements: •	Enable compatibility across multiple generations of building systems, from existing solutions (Generation 1) to future developments (Generation X). •	Ensure backward compatibility with previously deployed panel systems and connection concepts. •	Support standardized and interoperable interfaces to facilitate integration across different manufacturers, suppliers and construction systems. •	Enable modular extensions and upgrades throughout the building lifecycle. •	Allow integration of future material innovations, including emerging bio-based, recycled or advanced engineered materials. •	Accommodate different panel configurations, dimensions and assembly concepts without requiring fundamental redesign of the connection system. •	Support adaptable building designs and evolving construction requirements over time. •	Facilitate long-term system scalability while maintaining structural integrity and ease of assembly.
candidate.title: Austrian construction company seeks circular and demountable connection technology for load-bearing timber panel systems

candidate.description_text: The Austrian deep-tech startup (a university spin-off) builds on more than 25 years of expertise in electrolysers and fuel cells. The company specialises in developing and manufacturing cutting-edge Membrane Electrode Assembly (MEA) technology that powers the hydrogen economy. In line with its activities in the development and production of electrochemical energy components, the startup is looking for European partners with roll-to-roll manufacturing capacity. The company develops membrane electrode components used in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. These components include catalyst-coated membranes, catalyst-coated substrates and membrane electrode assemblies. The company currently builds its processes at laboratory and pilot scale and has access to a roll-to-roll pilot line for process validation and medium-volume production. After this validation step, external manufacturing capacity will be needed for larger and more regular production volumes. The purpose of this partner search is therefore to assess the availability of suitable European manufacturing capacity, including which capabilities are available, what technical limitations apply, and how cooperation could be structured. The external manufacturing need is expected from 2028 onwards. The required technology is roll-to-roll slot-die coating and related downstream processing for thin functional catalyst layers on flexible and, where possible, porous substrates. The preferred partner should be able to support not only coating but also drying, web handling, lamination, cutting or stamping, integration of gasket or subgasket materials, quality control, documentation and packaging. The expected production capacity is up to around 5,000 m² per year, depending on product mix and successful process transfer. The company is seeking cooperation with European industrial partners that already operate suitable roll-to-roll coating or converting lines, ideally with experience in functional coatings, electrochemical components, membranes, catalyst inks, fuel cells, electrolysers, batteries, sensors, printed electronics or comparable thin-film products. The minimum useful coating width is 300 mm; a width up to 800 mm would be ideal. Detailed coating formulations, layer structures, product drawings, process windows and customer-related specifications are confidential and would only be shared under a non-disclosure agreement and after an initial technical fit assessment. Cooperation could start with capability discussions and non-confidential process mapping, continue with feasibility trials and pilot campaigns, and later move into recurring manufacturing. The preferred cooperation types are an outsourcing agreement, a supplier agreement and, where process transfer or adaptation is needed, a commercial agreement with technical assistance.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner should be a European company, contract manufacturer or coating specialist operating roll-to-roll slot-die coating and converting equipment. The partner should first provide a non-confidential overview of its available line widths, coating technologies, compatible substrates, drying and lamination options, quality control methods, typical campaign sizes, available capacity and experience with functional coatings.
candidate.title: Seeking roll-to-roll slot-die manufacturing capacity for electrochemical membrane electrode components

candidate.description_text: Brussels-based energy technology company providing modular first-life LFP BESS together with a proprietary EMS and cloud analytics platform. The solution combines an integrated battery-and-energy management architecture with continuous monitoring and digital-twin-based analytics to optimize performance, reliability, and lifetime. Up to February 2026, 80 MW of smart-controlled flexible assets and manages 150 MWh of battery storage capacity, reflecting strong growth and a rapidly expanding position in the flexibility and storage market were operated by the company. Research is a core pillar of their activities to stay aligned with state-of-the-art methods and to shape future products based on market needs and emerging technologies. They are active in European (e.g., Horizon) and national R&D projects and focus on State-of-X topics (SoC/SoH), lifetime and Remaining Useful Life modelling and advanced EMS control for more efficient multi-asset power flow. Main products & services offered: • Hardware product: Modular Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) for the C&I segment ranging from 100 kWh to 5 MWh. •	Services o	Battery Care 	Detailed remote monitoring and automated alerting 	Troubleshooting in case of issues with the Battery System 	Warranty management o	Energy Management System (EMS) 	Self-consumption optimization 	Peak shaving 	Market arbitrage (day-ahead and imbalance markets) 	Grid services 	Value stacking of different applications
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Seeking industry partners and research centers to collaborate on its R&D roadmap and accelerate next-generation BESS and EMS innovation. The SME also aims to co-develop forecasting and smart control capabilities, including weather-condition–based forecasting, household consumption mapping, and AI-based control to optimize multi-asset power flow more efficiently.

candidate.description_text: This Belgian chocolate manufacturer has a long history behind its today's production, with longstanding expertise and craftmanship in every stage of chocolate making. They produce high-quality fine chocolates for branded manufacturers and for private labels and have built their reputation and the collaboration with their clients on a blended mix of creativity, innovation and quality. This results in a variety of fillings, shapes, molds, decorations. While wishing to keep all these characteristics  - which combine traditional skills and modern techniques - to deliver excellent products, they are confronted with the increasing of the production costs. Among the others, costs linked to the cocoa.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: In order to limit the impact of raw material prices, and notably cocoa, this Belgian company is actively looking for vegetable fat to be used as an alternative to cocoa in the filling of their large range of chocolates, chocolate bars, pralines, truffles etc. The vegetable fat alternative will be used in the filling of the chocolate pralines and has to guarantee the same density and easiness to work the product as for traditional pralines stuffed with cocoa. The cocoa would then be used only for the external coating. The vegetable fat alternative sought needs to: - be used directly in production, without melting step, - ideally come in 20kg (max 25kg) for proper handling - be easily combined with the coating, which can be of simple chocolate or eg a praline powdered or enrobed with nuts, fruits - easily embrace the shape, moulds selected for the production The filling with vegetable fat alternative must be : -	close the density of the pralines with a traditional cocoa filling -	FSSC 22000 certified: Guaranteed food safety and quality standards -	from sourced ingredients produced in Europe by suppliers located in Europe The potential partner must have track records in the manufacturing of the vegetable fat alternative sought

candidate.description_text: A Bulgarian deep-tech SME with long-standing expertise in geospatial technologies, surveying and infrastructure monitoring has developed a protected software-led autonomous air-water inspection and mapping technology. The technology is designed to bridge the operational gap between above-water and underwater surveying by combining observations from both environments into a single georeferenced operational model. Potential applications include dams and hydraulic structures, ports and harbour infrastructure, bridges, underwater pipelines and cables, coastal erosion and sediment monitoring, marine environmental monitoring, and underwater cultural heritage documentation. The software architecture, data-processing environment and artificial intelligence perception layer have already been developed. The current stage focuses on integration with real underwater hardware and validation in operational missions. The company is seeking European technology and industrial partners capable of providing, adapting or integrating an open and customisable underwater robotic platform. Relevant capabilities include payload capacity, onboard electrical power and thermal management for edge computing, access to vehicle telemetry and raw sensor data, documented software interfaces, and integration of customer-selected navigation, sonar, bathymetric and environmental sensors. Cooperation may involve integration with an existing commercially available underwater vehicle, adaptation of a platform for customer-supplied onboard computing and sensing equipment, physical and electrical integration, prototype manufacturing, laboratory and field testing, pilot validation and preparation for commercial deployment. The Bulgarian company retains ownership of its protected software, artificial intelligence, algorithms, system architecture and integration know-how. The expected partner contribution concerns complementary underwater hardware, manufacturing, physical integration, testing, validation and/or investment supporting market deployment.

Depending on its capabilities, the partner may: •	provide a commercially available open and customisable underwater robotic platform; •	adapt an existing platform for customer-supplied onboard computing and sensors; •	provide sufficient electrical power, payload capacity and thermal management for edge computing; •	provide documented access to telemetry, navigation data, raw sensor data and vehicle interfaces; •	integrate customer-selected sonar, navigation, bathymetric or environmental sensors; •	perform physical, mechanical and electrical integration; •	manufacture prototype mechanical or pressure-resistant components; •	support laboratory, field and pilot validation; •	participate in preparation for commercial deployment; •	or provide strategic investment supporting hardware integration, validation and market entry. The Bulgarian company will retain responsibility for its proprietary software, artificial intelligence, data-processing and system-level integration technology.

candidate.description_text: Founded with the mission to accelerate the transition to a circular economy, a Swiss startup specializing in sustainable industrial chemistry and eco-friendly additive development leverages advanced material science to transform industrial waste streams into valuable manufacturing inputs. Operating with a lean structure and cutting-edge vision, the organization focuses on developing scalable, green chemical solutions that mitigate the environmental footprint of traditional manufacturing materials. The company seeks manufacturers of rubber goods or industrial organization to co-develop and scale up rubber recycling through a more sustainable devulcanization process. The global vulcanized rubber industry faces a severe waste management challenge. Traditional vulcanization creates permanent, crosslinked sulfur bonds within the rubber matrix. These bonds make the material durable but also difficult to recycle. Standard mechanical grinding merely downgrades the material into low-value filler, while incineration and landfilling create significant environmental liabilities. To solve this problem, the startup offers a high-performance eco-friendly chemical additive for rubber devulcanization. The product functions via a gentle chemical-mechanical process that targets and breaks down the sulfur-sulfur crosslinks while preserving the integrity of the main polymer chains. The resulting material acts as a functional secondary raw material that retains the inherent elastomeric or abrasion properties of the original feedstock. While not all recovered rubber is highly formulated, preserving the original compound's existing additives in highly compounded inputs - like tires - allows manufacturers to optimize formulations and reduce the volume of new chemical inputs. While the chemical formulation is available, the core problem to be solved lies in its end-user application. The startup requires advanced end-user technical manufacturing know-how and material testing capabilities. Specifically, the technology requested involves the practical application, compounding, and performance validation of the devulcanized material when it is blended back into new product lines. Collaboration with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization seeking sustainable technologies to recycle their rubber waste would allow to determine how the treated rubber behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it seamlessly integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final structural integrity. Transitioning a chemical formulation into a successful, commercial-grade end product requires a collaborative feedback loop between the chemical developer and the material manufacturer. Technical cooperation or joint venture with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization is thought: to co-develop optimized blending guidelines and successful manufacture market-ready consumer or technical rubber goods containing high percentages of recycled material. Unlike conventional high-temperature devulcanization methods, our chemical-mechanical process operates efficiently under reduced thermal requirements without demanding high-heat inputs, lowering energy consumption. By providing a substitute for resource-intensive virgin materials, this method inherently drives a substantial reduction in the overall process carbon footprint. Cooperation throught: commercial agreements, or joint development projects (Eurostars or Horizon Europe) if mutually beneficial. Partners are expected to provide industrial testing environments, product compounding expertise, and quality assurance evaluation for the final rubber products. The start up is also open to joint venture or partnership that support both the validation of the innovation and the integration of recycled  rubber materials into new goods or consumer products.

description_text: Founded with the mission to accelerate the transition to a circular economy, a Swiss startup specializing in sustainable industrial chemistry and eco-friendly additive development leverages advanced material science to transform industrial waste streams into valuable manufacturing inputs. Operating with a lean structure and cutting-edge vision, the organization focuses on developing scalable, green chemical solutions that mitigate the environmental footprint of traditional manufacturing materials. The company seeks manufacturers of rubber goods or industrial organization to co-develop and scale up rubber recycling through a more sustainable devulcanization process. The global vulcanized rubber industry faces a severe waste management challenge. Traditional vulcanization creates permanent, crosslinked sulfur bonds within the rubber matrix. These bonds make the material durable but also difficult to recycle. Standard mechanical grinding merely downgrades the material into low-value filler, while incineration and landfilling create significant environmental liabilities. To solve this problem, the startup offers a high-performance eco-friendly chemical additive for rubber devulcanization. The product functions via a gentle chemical-mechanical process that targets and breaks down the sulfur-sulfur crosslinks while preserving the integrity of the main polymer chains. The resulting material acts as a functional secondary raw material that retains the inherent elastomeric or abrasion properties of the original feedstock. While not all recovered rubber is highly formulated, preserving the original compound's existing additives in highly compounded inputs - like tires - allows manufacturers to optimize formulations and reduce the volume of new chemical inputs. While the chemical formulation is available, the core problem to be solved lies in its end-user application. The startup requires advanced end-user technical manufacturing know-how and material testing capabilities. Specifically, the technology requested involves the practical application, compounding, and performance validation of the devulcanized material when it is blended back into new product lines. Collaboration with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization seeking sustainable technologies to recycle their rubber waste would allow to determine how the treated rubber behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it seamlessly integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final structural integrity. Technical cooperation or joint venture with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization is thought: to co-develop optimized blending guidelines and successful manufacture market-ready consumer or technical rubber goods containing high percentages of recycled material. Unlike conventional high-temperature devulcanization methods, our chemical-mechanical process operates efficiently under reduced thermal requirements without demanding high-heat inputs, lowering energy consumption. By providing a substitute for resource-intensive virgin materials, this method inherently drives a substantial reduction in the overall process carbon footprint. Cooperation throught: commercial agreements, or joint development projects (Eurostars or Horizon Europe) if mutually beneficial. Partners are expected to provide industrial testing environments, product compounding expertise, and quality assurance evaluation for the final rubber products. The start up is also open to joint venture or partnership that support both the validation of the innovation and the integration of recycled  rubber materials into new goods or consumer products.

candidate.description_text: A Swiss organisation linked to the Geneva Forum and the Geneva Foundation for the Future is seeking user organisations worldwide to test, use and deploy the impact finance evaluation framework AGILE within real decision-making processes. The request concerns practical integration to further evaluate both its usage methodology and its effectiveness in project assessment, not the development of a new tool. AGILE is an impact finance evaluation framework designed to help users identify, assess, mentor, monitor and scale impact-driven initiatives. It provides a shared grammar between philanthropy, investment, public institutions, project leaders and academic actors, and can be applied to project pipelines, grantmaking, impact investment selection, public funding schemes, blended finance, CSR/ESG (Corporate Social Responsibility/ Environmental, Social, and Governance) transition, incubation, portfolio review, education and training. The framework is structured around five functional pillars: - Alignment with values, SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals), ESG/GRI (Global Reporting Initiative) standards and local realities; - Governance based on participation, transparency and accountability; - Intention focused on deep, structural and systemic impact; - Leadership able to mobilise and sustain change; - Efficiency in resource use, economic viability and scalability. The sought partners are organisations willing to pilot AGILE on real cases, compare it with their existing criteria and explore its deployment in their own processes. The collaboration may start with a limited pilot, workshop or use case, then progress to internal training, portfolio integration, platform adaptation or broader deployment. AGILE is a methodological and decision-support framework. Its use does not replace financial, legal or investment advice.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partners sought should be organisations able to test or deploy AGILE in at least one real operational process. No specific technology stack is required for a first pilot. Digital integration, API connection, data import/export or dashboard adaptation can be discussed after the initial use case.

candidate.description_text: The applicant is a German SME operating in structured content production and multi-format publishing. Over the last four years the company has developed a semantic anchoring system that gives every relevant text element in an editable office-format document a persistent identifier. References stay attached to their content when documents are restructured, edited under change tracking or export-ed to several output channels in parallel. Per document the system handles between 3,000 and 9,000 anchored references. The system has been in productive use in the company's own editorial domain since late 2024. The intended cooperation moves the technology into a different field: regulated technical documentation for medical devices under MDR 2017/745. References in that field are not editorial. A symbol, a warning, a product identifier or a clinical claim carries regulatory weight, and it has to stay consistent through the whole product life cycle, through up to 24 language versions, and through every audit a Notified Body decides to run. Tools used today in this market rely either on rigid component content management, on manual reference maintenance, or on layout workflows that lose semantic links somewhere between a translation round and a release approval. The company has seen no toolchain that solves this without trade-offs. The project builds on the existing anchoring technology but requires substantial experimental development. Unresolved technical challenges concern the preservation of regulatory meaning across structural edits, multilingual transformations, terminology changes, redlining and controlled release processes. On top of this sit integration with translation memory and controlled terminology; audit trails that satisfy ISO 13485 change-control duties and MDR Annex II documentation requirements; mechanisms that carry the regulatory weight of a reference through translation, redlining and release; and validation methods that generate evidence suitable for review during quality-management and conformity-assessment audits. The cooperation delivers a demonstrator validated against real cases from the partner, plus an evaluation framework for regulatory fit. The cooperation is designed for the German ZIM cooperative project track. Each side runs its own work packages and holds its own grant share. The company brings running technology, software-side R&D capacity and document-structure expertise. The partner brings the regulated domain and contributes its own regulatory-methodological R&D work packages — among them the development of a formal regulatory reference model, risk-based validation criteria, multilingual compliance rules, and methods for verifying reference integrity across document revisions, translations and release processes. The parties intend to conclude a research and development cooperation agreement for the planned project. Rights to pre-existing technology, jointly developed results and subsequent exploitation will be regulated in a project-specific cooperation agreement.

The partner brings the regulated domain the applicant does not have in-house. Required: •	active responsibility for medical device documentation under MDR 2017/745 (instructions for use, technical documentation, labelling, clinical content); •	working knowledge of ISO 13485 quality management, in particular document and change control; •	practical experience with multilingual release, translation memory and controlled terminology; •	practical experience with audits and conformity-assessment procedures involving Notified Bodies (an institutional link to a Notified Body is not required); •	own R&D capacity to define regulatory acceptance criteria, co-develop the regulatory reference model and validation methodology, and run its own work packages; •	ability to name concrete validation scenarios, document structures and bottlenecks from current practice; •	willingness to provide realistic sample content (anonymised where required) for demonstrator validation; •	readiness to enter a formal cooperation under the German ZIM cooperative project track. The semantic anchoring base technology is in production in the applicant's own domain. For the MedTech application the work is at concept stage: the regulatory extension, the terminology integration and the audit-trail validation are the subject of the cooperation. A working demonstration of the base mechanism is available under NDA.

candidate.description_text: The Danish SME develops reusable container solutions for catering and takeaway with the objective of reducing single‑use packaging and improving circular return systems. To support efficient return logistics, the company is seeking a technology capable of reliable single‑item identification of reusable food containers (e.g. bowls, plates, trays). The containers are manufactured from a wood‑plastic composite (WPC) material and are designed for repeated reuse under demanding operational conditions. They must withstand industrial dishwashing, microwave heating, oven exposure and freezing without degradation. Any identification solution must tolerate the same conditions over the product lifetime. The purpose of the identification technology is to enable operational tracking and identification during use and return cycles (e.g. in catering kitchens and return facilities). The solution is not consumer‑facing and does not require anti‑counterfeiting or brand protection features. A key operational requirement is that containers cannot be guaranteed a fixed orientation during scanning. The requested technology must therefore be orientation‑independent, either through surface‑wide identification or through identification principles that do not rely on a predefined code position. Containers are scanned in two main environments: Small‑scale or decentralised operations using standard smartphones High‑volume kitchens using fixed or tunnel‑mounted industrial camera systems The company is not seeking a full end‑to‑end tracking platform, but rather access to the core identification technology (e.g. algorithm, SDK (Software Development Kit), or licensable method) that can be integrated into its own backend systems. Material‑intrinsic identification The container material has a naturally heterogeneous surface structure, with visible wood fibres distributed randomly. This inherent variability means that no two containers are identical, opening the possibility of identification based on the material itself. Solutions based on surface fingerprinting or material‑intrinsic identification, where the natural surface structure is captured (e.g. optically) and used as a unique identifier are therefore of strong interest, provided they can reliably identify individual containers over the full product lifetime despite normal wear and cleaning.

candidate.description_text: The company is a Spanish technology startup developing data infrastructure and analytics solutions for complex energy markets. The organisation focuses on improving how investment decisions are made in renewable energy systems by integrating fragmented operational and market data into decision-ready intelligence tools. Across European electricity markets, renewable energy investment decisions depend on multiple datasets that are typically fragmented across different sources. Market prices, grid connection constraints, infrastructure pipelines, weather data, regulatory developments and auction rules are often accessed through separate platforms, public portals or consultancy reports. Analysts and investment teams frequently combine these sources manually using spreadsheets and disconnected tools. This process is time-consuming, difficult to standardise across markets and can lead to incomplete or inconsistent analysis. Existing solutions in the market usually focus on specific analytical domains. Some platforms provide electricity market forecasts or price modelling tools, while others offer renewable resource datasets, grid information portals or consultancy-based market reports. However, these solutions rarely integrate all relevant intelligence layers required for renewable infrastructure investment decisions within a single analytical environment. The proposed technology addresses this gap by providing an integrated data and analytics platform designed to combine key intelligence layers for renewable energy markets. The platform aggregates structured data from multiple sources, including electricity market prices, transmission system operator data, renewable resource indicators, regulatory information and infrastructure development pipelines. Through a unified data architecture and analytical interface, users can analyse market conditions, compare investment opportunities across regions and evaluate potential project revenues and risks. The platform supports applications such as opportunity screening for solar, wind and energy storage projects, identification of attractive bidding zones, and simulation of potential revenue streams for battery energy storage systems under different market conditions. The technology is designed to support organisations operating in complex energy environments, including renewable energy developers, utilities, energy traders, infrastructure investors and energy consultancies. The company is currently in the technology validation phase and is seeking international partners for research and development cooperation. The aim is to validate and further develop the platform through pilot projects in real operational or analytical environments across European electricity markets. Partners are expected to provide access to relevant data, use cases or testing environments, and to contribute to the assessment of the platform’s performance and applicability. The cooperation would support the adaptation of the solution to different market conditions and the preparation for wider commercial deployment.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking cooperation with organisations operating in European electricity and renewable energy markets that are interested in testing and applying the technology within real analytical, operational or investment environments. Potential partners may include renewable energy developers, utilities, energy trading organisations, infrastructure investors, asset operators, energy consultancies or research institutions working on electricity market analysis, forecasting and energy system modelling. The expected cooperation may include pilot deployments of the platform to support renewable energy investment analysis, operational optimisation and validation of analytical models using real project data. This includes joint exploration of use cases related to solar, wind or battery energy storage projects, as well as the application of the platform’s Forecast functionality. The Forecast functionality is designed to allow operators to enhance their existing forecasting models and strengthen market participation. By testing operator-provided forecasts against the data and analytical capabilities available within the platform, the tool can assess whether platform data, enhanced modelling and weather-based adjustments could improve forecasting accuracy and operational performance. This functionality is intended to help operators validate decisionmaking processes, identify potential forecast improvements and reinforce participation strategies in power markets. Partners may contribute expertise related to specific electricity markets, grid infrastructure planning, regulatory analysis, forecasting practices or energy project development. Collaboration could also involve joint development of additional analytical modules, validation of forecast optimisation approaches, or the integration of new data sources relevant to regional energy markets and asset performance. The objective of the cooperation is to validate and further develop the platform while enabling partners to improve their ability to analyse market opportunities, assess infrastructure constraints, optimise forecasting performance and evaluate potential revenue streams for renewable energy projects.

candidate.description_text: The company is building a new infrastructure layer for the impact economy, addressing one of the biggest gaps in sustainability today: the lack of verifiable, trustworthy and auditable impact data. Current ESG reporting is fragmented, declarative and difficult to validate. Organizations struggle to demonstrate that their actions generate real, measurable outcomes, creating a critical trust gap between companies, institutions and stakeholders. The company addresses this challenge by transforming real-world problems into structured, traceable and verifiable impact through a unified system. At the core of this system is Impact Graph, a structured workflow engine that enables organizations to transform ideas, decisions, projects or initiatives into verifiable processes. It supports: - the decomposition of actions into structured workflows - the attachment of real evidence (documents, links, files) - the generation of structured records - the creation of traceable timelines - the preparation of projects for external verification This approach turns intention into structured evidence. The platform combines : - A discovery layer where ideas, initiatives and projects emerge and are validated by the community - Impact Graph for structuring workflows and preparing projects for verification and funding - AI-driven analysis to guide decisions and execution - A traceability layer to record decisions, processes and evidence - A data integrity layer ensuring structured and verifiable information - A blockchain anchoring layer securing checkpoints and proofs - Proof-of-Impact mechanisms to certify and validate real-world outcomes Together, these components create a complete system in which every step—from problem identification to funding readiness—is structured, traceable and verifiable. This enables a new flow : problem → solution → initiative → structured workflow → evidence → verification → funding readiness The system is designed as a distributed infrastructure capable of operating locally (including in offline environments) and synchronizing with global networks. This architecture enables deployment across sectors such as energy, manufacturing, smart buildings, healthcare and sustainable infrastructure. Use cases include: - Impact measurement and certification for ESG and sustainability programs - Structuring projects to access grants and funding - Community-driven initiatives and crowdfunding with verifiable outcomes - Operational traceability in industrial environments - Energy monitoring and optimization - Transparent reporting for institutions, corporates and public-sector actors By bridging the gap between real-world actions and digital verification, the company enables organizations to move from declarative ESG reporting to measurable, auditable and trusted impact. The long-term vision is to establish Proof‑of‑Impact as a global standard for how impact is structured, verified and trusted. The company aims to provide a system that structures, verifies and certifies impact from end to end.

candidate.description_text: A pioneer in the field of natural bee products, the French company seeks to develop a new propolis processing technology based on supercritical CO₂ extraction. The aim is to selectively recover compounds of interest, particularly polyphenols, flavonoids, Artepillin C, and Biochanin A, while separating undesirable substances such as pesticide residues, heavy metals, and PAHs. This process will make it possible to “decontaminate” propolis and obtain purer, better standardized extracts with improved quality and safety. It also will also address the need to diversify dosage forms, with the development of liquid extracts richer in active compounds or alternatives to traditional alcohol-based extracts, which are often highly concentrated in alcohol that has a negative effect on their aromatic properties. The company, therefore, is looking to identify a partner with proven expertise in supercritical extraction, selective separation of natural compounds, and process optimisation for complex matrices. The desired collaboration could take the form of a research and development partnership or commercial agreement with technical support for process development, optimisation, and validation. The ultimate objective is to enhance the value of propolis, improve its analytical quality, and develop new high value-added natural ingredients suitable for applications in dietary supplements, natural health products, or aromatic formulations.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The right partner is expected to have strong expertise in supercritical CO₂ extraction processes applied to natural raw materials, ideally oils, resins, aromatic plants, or complex matrices comparable to propolis. Expertise in separating and extracting large molecules such as pesticides, heavy metals, and PAHs would be an advantage. Strong capabilities in selective fractionation, process parameter optimisation, and contaminant reduction are required. The targeted know-how includes in particular: - Selection of pressure, temperature, and potential co-solvent parameters - Separation of target compounds from lipophilic or semi-volatile contaminants - Recovery of fractions rich in polyphenols and flavonoids - Evaluation of decontamination efficiency regarding pesticides and PAHs - Development of low-alcohol or alcohol-free extracts - Possible scale-up to pilot or pre-industrial level This would require establishing a comprehensive experimental design to minimise the cost of trials.

It is looking for a research and development cooperation agreement

candidate.description_text: The French SME is a pioneer and technology leader in high-quality imaging systems, with deep expertise in designing high-performance cameras specifically engineered for underwater and industrial applications, including operations in highly turbid or low-visibility waters. As part of its strategic expansion to deliver advanced subsea inspection capabilities, the company is seeking an expert partner in software-based 3D reconstruction. The collaborative goal is to co-develop a robust 3D modeling and reconstruction software solution specifically adapted to challenging underwater optical conditions and designed to ingest the video streams produced by the French company's proprietary cameras. The ultimate ambition is to market a distinctive, non-intrusive solution enabling high-precision integrity monitoring and wear control of submerged offshore infrastructure. Targeted application areas include anchor chains, flexible joints on pipelines, immersed metallic structures, fittings, and specific corrosion or wear zones on marine assets. Depending on the partner's technology maturity, cooperation will be established through a Research and Development Cooperation Agreement or a Commercial Agreement with Technical Assistance.

candidate.description_text: We are a UK-based SME developing a novel immunomodulatory platform based on programmable, genome-inactivated Bacteria-Like Particles (BLiPs). Using proprietary bioinformatics and synthetic biology, the company generates fully inactivated, non-replicative bacterial cells that retain native surface antigens and pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), enabling potent immune stimulation with an enhanced safety profile. The BLiP platform overcomes key limitations of conventional bacterial inactivation methods and subunit vaccine approaches while providing a versatile platform for prophylactic and immunomodulatory applications. The company is advancing two lead programmes. The first is an intranasal prophylactic vaccine against recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs), targeting uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) to induce protective mucosal immunity. The second is a broad-spectrum innate immune trainer for respiratory diseases, designed to establish a pre-emptive antiviral state within the respiratory mucosa and provide pathogen-agnostic protection against emerging and seasonal respiratory viruses. In parallel, we offer genome inactivation services for custom bacterial targets, supporting the development of safe bacterial products and research tools. We seek international R&D collaborations with academic, CRO, and industrial partners possessing established in vitro and/or in vivo UTI models, human airway or immune models, and respiratory infection challenge models. Collaborations will involve joint study design, evaluation of BLiP-based candidates in partner models, and shared data generation to validate efficacy, mechanism of action, and translational potential. The desired outcome is to establish robust preclinical proof-of-concept for both lead programmes while demonstrating the broader applicability of the BLiP platform.

candidate.description_text: Two UK SMEs are forming a European consortium for a proposed EIT Urban Mobility Strategic Innovation Open Call project. The company has already sourced the core optical components, including camera modules and lenses, and is currently seeking a specialized technical partner or system integrator capable of undertaking the full hardware integration and industrialization process of the platform. Furthermore, the platform must support seamless interoperability with existing vessel systems and communication infrastructure, enabling efficient transmission of synchronized multispectral video streams and metadata to external AI-based processing environments and command systems. candidate.description_text: A Greek SME develops and markets handmade cosmetic skincare products, including serums, eye creams, sunscreen products, cream bases and active ingredient-based formulations. The company’s approach focuses on personalised skincare solutions adapted to the specific needs of each skin type, avoiding unnecessarily complex skincare routines. Building on this activity, the company is developing an advanced, patent-pending dermocosmetic delivery system for topical cosmetic applications. The system is designed to support the stabilisation and synchronised, multi-phase release of sensitive active ingredients, including nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, commonly known as NAD+, and targeted signalling peptides. The product has reached a stage where external laboratory testing is needed to assess the skin penetration and distribution profile of NAD+ as a selected marker under controlled in vitro conditions. The requested study should evaluate the penetration potential of NAD+ using a reconstructed human epidermis model under physiological conditions and provide quantitative evidence on the behaviour of the marker after topical application. The study is expected to result in a comprehensive technical report, including data analysis and statistical evaluation. The company is seeking a specialised skin penetration testing laboratory, dermal absorption laboratory, bioanalytical laboratory, contract research organisation, research institute or university laboratory able to provide the requested testing service under a commercial agreement with technical assistance. The company is expecting the final results to be delivered by 31 October 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking a specialised skin penetration testing laboratory, dermal absorption laboratory, bioanalytical laboratory, contract research organisation, research institute or university laboratory with proven experience in in vitro percutaneous penetration, dermal absorption or transdermal delivery studies. The partner should have the necessary equipment, validated methods and scientific expertise to work with reconstructed human epidermis models and topical cosmetic or dermocosmetic formulations under physiological conditions. Experience with Franz diffusion cells or equivalent in vitro penetration testing systems would be highly relevant. The partner should also have the analytical capacity to quantify NAD+ or comparable bioactive markers in biological or reconstructed tissue-based samples, preferably using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) or another suitable validated analytical method. Experience in cosmetic, dermocosmetic, pharmaceutical, transdermal or bioanalytical testing is a prerequisite.

candidate.description_text: This Hungarian SME specializes in the development of advanced wildfire prevention and mitigation systems. Based on several years of multidisciplinary research, the company has developed three patented inventions to enhance forest fire resilience. The core technology functions by coating tree trunks within a designated protection zone with a proprietary, highly viscous, water-cooling chemical formulation. This coating prevents the bark from heating to its ignition threshold, effectively creating an active firebreak to halt the spread of wildfires. While the chemical formulation and core principles have been validated in laboratory environments, the company requires external technical capabilities to transition from a "pilot-ready" status to large-scale, field-ready deployment. Specifically, the company lacks the heavy mechanical platforms and automated spray-applicators required to distribute the fluid formulation efficiently across uneven and densely forested terrain. To bridge this gap, the Hungarian company is seeking international partners to contribute specialized engineering expertise, heavy-machinery platforms, and automated sensing systems to co-develop a mobile wildfire-suppression prototype. The client seeks to establish partnerships under two distinct frameworks. Research and Development Cooperation Agreement: •	To combine the company's patented chemical concept with external engineering expertise to design, build, and test a fully functional physical prototype. •	Partners will collaborate on mechanical and hydraulic integration, fluid dynamics modeling for high-viscosity distribution, and the execution of joint field trials to validate performance in real-world environments. Commercial Agreement with Technical Assistance: •	To adapt existing high-mobility forestry machinery or agricultural mobile platforms to serve as the carrier vehicle for the distribution system. •	The partner will supply or adapt off-the-shelf machinery, integrated sensors, or control systems and provide the necessary technical documentation and operational training to the Hungarian development team.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian organisation experienced in European innovation and technology-development projects is building cooperation opportunities for Horizon Europe and other future EU-funded projects in the field of e-fuel-compatible marine propulsion. The organisation is seeking an engine or propulsion-system manufacturer established in an EU Member State that has already developed an engine, generator-based propulsion package or hybrid system capable of operating on one or more synthetic e-fuels. In the European Union context, the term e-fuel generally refers to a synthetic gaseous or liquid fuel produced using renewable electricity. Renewable electricity is typically used to produce renewable hydrogen through electrolysis. This hydrogen can then be combined with captured carbon dioxide or, for certain fuels, nitrogen to produce synthetic fuels. Examples may include: * e-methanol; * e-methane; * e-diesel; * e-ammonia; * other renewable hydrogen-derived synthetic fuels. In EU policy and legislation, many such fuels are classified as renewable fuels of non-biological origin, or RFNBOs, provided that they comply with the applicable requirements concerning renewable electricity, production pathways and greenhouse-gas-emission savings. For this partner search, an e-fuel-capable propulsion system means an engine or integrated powertrain that is designed, demonstrated, certified or technically adaptable to operate on a qualifying synthetic fuel produced mainly from renewable electricity rather than directly from fossil feedstocks. The proposed technology must have reached at least Technology Readiness Level 6 and should already exist as a functional prototype, integrated propulsion system or pre-commercial product demonstrated in a relevant environment. The sought solution may include: * internal-combustion engines capable of operating on e-methanol; * engines compatible with e-methane or synthetic methane; * engines capable of using synthetic diesel or e-diesel; * ammonia-capable engines where the fuel pathway is based on renewable hydrogen; * dual-fuel or multi-fuel engines; * e-fuel-electric hybrid propulsion; * generator-based propulsion systems using e-fuels; * engines combined with batteries, electric motors or energy-management systems; * conversion or retrofit technologies enabling an existing engine platform to operate on an e-fuel. The proposed propulsion system must be designed for, used in, or capable of being adapted to marine operating conditions, including exposure to moisture, saltwater, corrosion, vibration, temperature variation and demanding duty cycles. The cooperation is not intended to support the development of a new engine from the initial concept stage. The selected company should already own, manufacture or have the documented legal right to develop and commercialise the proposed technology. Potential cooperation activities may include: * adaptation of an existing engine to one or more e-fuels; * fuel-system and combustion-system optimisation; * improvement of efficiency, emissions and operational reliability; * development of dual-fuel or multi-fuel operating modes; * integration with electric propulsion, batteries or generators; * optimisation of control and energy-management systems; * adaptation to additional marine configurations; * validation and demonstration in relevant operating conditions; * preparation for certification and regulatory compliance; * industrialisation and market deployment. The exact fuel pathway, propulsion configuration and development activities will be defined jointly with the selected manufacturer under suitable Horizon Europe topics or other relevant EU funding opportunities. Due to the commercially sensitive nature of the planned initiative, details concerning the wider project concept, cooperation structure, intended applications and proposed activities will not be disclosed publicly.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian non-profit innovation and technology organisation is developing an interregional investment project proposal under the I3-2026-INV2a – Financial and advisory support for investments in interregional innovation projects for the development of value chains in less developed regions, Strand 2a call. The project aims to establish and demonstrate a new European value chain for the production of large rotationally moulded HDPE components. The envisaged products will be intended primarily for demanding outdoor and marine-related applications, although the production technology may also be used for large components in aquaculture, infrastructure, transport, agriculture, environmental technologies and other industrial sectors. The consortium is looking for a machinery manufacturer, engineering company or industrial technology developer capable of designing and delivering a large-scale rotational moulding production system. The equipment must be suitable for manufacturing components with approximate maximum dimensions of: Length: 6.5 metres Width: 2.5 metres Height: 1.5 metres A rock-and-roll rotational moulding machine is currently considered a potentially appropriate solution because of the intended component size and geometry. However, the consortium is open to other configurations, provided that the proposed machinery can reliably and economically manufacture components of the required dimensions and quality. The machinery must be designed to process virgin and recycled HDPE. Particular importance is placed on the ability to accommodate recycled HDPE feedstock, including material with greater variability in melt behaviour, particle distribution and processing characteristics than standard virgin rotational-moulding powder. The project partner should therefore be able to develop or adapt the machinery, heating system, mould movement, process controls and material-feeding concept to ensure consistent production when using: * virgin HDPE powder; * recycled HDPE powder; * blends of virgin and recycled HDPE; * potentially HDPE granulate, where a technically feasible granulate-based or in-line material-preparation solution is proposed; * multilayer structures containing different virgin and recycled-HDPE formulations. The final machinery should support the production of large components with controlled wall thickness, adequate fusion, limited porosity, repeatable mechanical properties and consistent dimensional accuracy. The selected partner will be expected to participate actively in the technical development, engineering, production, installation, commissioning and industrial validation of the machinery. The current technology stage should be at least on :  TRL 6 level and are expected to progress towards industrial deployment. The applicable funding rate is: 70% European Commission funding; 30% own contribution by the project partner. The prospective partner must therefore have sufficient financial capacity to provide its share of project co-financing and sufficient operational capacity to complete the machinery development and delivery.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian non-profit innovation and technology organisation is developing cooperation opportunities in the field of large rotationally moulded polymer products. The organisation is interested in new materials, manufacturing approaches and structural solutions that can reduce the weight and material consumption of rotationally moulded HDPE parts without compromising their mechanical strength, durability or long-term performance. The intended applications include large components for demanding outdoor and marine-related environments. The developed solutions may also be relevant to aquaculture, transport, infrastructure, agriculture, environmental technologies, energy systems and other sectors using large rotationally moulded products. One of the principal technical challenges is the relatively high material consumption and weight of large rotationally moulded components. Reducing wall thickness alone can result in insufficient stiffness, reduced impact resistance, excessive deformation, lower creep resistance and limited long-term durability. The organisation is therefore seeking innovative technologies that improve the strength-to-weight ratio of rotationally moulded products. Potential solutions may include, but are not limited to: * new virgin or recycled HDPE blends; * modified polyethylene formulations; * lightweight mineral, organic or recycled fillers; * short- or long-fibre reinforcement; * glass, basalt, carbon, natural or recycled fibres; * internal reinforcement meshes or textile structures; * embedded structural elements compatible with rotational moulding; * multilayer rotational moulding; * foamed-core or sandwich structures; * chemical or physical foaming technologies; * local reinforcement of highly loaded areas; * structural ribs or integrated internal geometries; * hybrid polymer structures; * additives improving stiffness, impact resistance or creep performance; * compatibilisers for recycled or mixed-polymer formulations; * nanomaterials or functional additives; * technologies enabling thinner but stronger walls; * simulation and optimisation tools supporting lightweight component design. The organisation is open to solutions based on HDPE and to compatible polymer systems that can be processed by rotational moulding or integrated into rotationally moulded products. Particular interest is placed on solutions compatible with recycled HDPE, including technologies that compensate for the variability, degradation or lower mechanical performance often associated with recycled feedstock. The intended components may be exposed to prolonged outdoor use, direct sunlight, elevated temperatures, humidity, saltwater and continuous mechanical loading. The organisation is therefore is also seeking technologies that improve: * resistance to ultraviolet radiation; * retention of tensile, flexural and impact properties after UV exposure; * colour and surface stability; * resistance to oxidation and embrittlement; * dimensional stability at elevated temperatures; * creep resistance under sustained loads; * resistance to thermal cycling; * resistance to combined UV, heat, humidity and saltwater exposure; * long-term durability in Mediterranean, tropical and other hot-climate environments. The organisation is particularly interested in technologies that address the combined effects of UV radiation, elevated surface temperature, environmental exposure and mechanical loading.

The proposed solution should address one or more of the following challenges: * reduction of component weight; * reduction of HDPE material consumption; * improvement of stiffness-to-weight ratio; * improvement of tensile, flexural or impact properties; * improved creep resistance; * reinforcement of large unsupported surfaces; * improved dimensional stability; * improved performance of recycled HDPE; * reduced deformation in hot climates; * improved UV resistance; * improved resistance to ageing and embrittlement; * improved long-term outdoor performance; * development of multilayer or sandwich structures; * development of reinforced or foamed rotationally moulded parts; * compatibility with industrial rotational moulding processes. The technology should be supported by available evidence such as: * laboratory test results; * prototype samples; * material data sheets; * accelerated ageing results; * mechanical testing results; * proof-of-concept demonstrators; * pilot applications; * patents or protected know-how; * scientific publications; * technical validation reports. Technologies existing only as theoretical concepts, without laboratory validation, are outside the scope of the request.

candidate.description_text: Malta-based company, an NVIDIA Inception member and founded by peer-reviewed AI researchers with MSc-level AI qualifications from the University of Malta, develops custom AI engineering for organisations that need a production AI system built to their specific operational requirements rather than fitted to an off-the-shelf product. The service offered to clients covers the complete delivery path from initial assessment through to production deployment. Engagements typically begin with an AI readiness assessment: identifying where AI fits in the client's workflows, evaluating data quality and structure, and scoping the build. From there, the team designs and delivers a system against those requirements, staying through stabilisation rather than handing over at go-live. Past work spans real-time camera analytics on edge devices, AI-assisted tools in educational environments, automated quantitative systems in financial contexts, and computer vision pipelines for industrial settings with all deployments sharing the same engineering standard: production-grade, compliant by architecture, and maintained on infrastructure the client controls. Compliance is embedded from the first design decision with GDPR and EU AI Act requirements addressed in architecture, not added at the end. Audit trails, access controls and human review checkpoints, are scoped into the system design, not appended before sign-off. Company can contribute on sovereign AI engineering capability including computer vision, edge inference, predictive analytics, and on-premise deployment architecture. The partner is to contribute on domain expertise, relevant datasets, sector regulatory context, and end-user relationships.

candidate.description_text: This Dutch deep-tech SME is active in the field of quantum technology and structural health monitoring, and is developing a patented surface coating that can turn everyday structures such as aircraft, bridges, wind turbines, ships and industrial equipment into continuous, contactless sensors. The technology requested is access to a laboratory with an operational setup for a specialised optical-magnetic measurement technique used to characterise microscopic defects in diamond material. This know-how and equipment is needed because the company has completed an extensive computational modelling programme, using five independent simulation tools across 22 separate studies, and the final missing step before physical proof-of-concept is a single, clearly defined laboratory measurement on coated diamond plate samples that the company will supply, together with a measurement protocol. Specifically, the technique requested is optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond. The coating is diamond-based and is sensitive, at a quantum level, to temperature, mechanical strain and magnetic fields. This information can be read out simply by illuminating the surface with light — remotely and without any physical contact. In this way, the entire coated surface becomes a sensor, without the need for wiring or embedded electronics, allowing early detection of micro-damage long before it would be visible through conventional inspection. Compared with conventional structural health monitoring — discrete, wired sensors that each measure a single parameter at fixed points — the coating measures temperature, strain and magnetic fields simultaneously, across the entire coated surface. To the company's knowledge, no current player combines quantum-grade sensing with a deployable structural coating. The desired outcome of an international partnership is to obtain independent, credible experimental confirmation that the coating performs as the simulations predict, which would allow the company to move toward licensing the technology to European industrial partners in aerospace, coatings and infrastructure monitoring. International cooperation is envisaged as a short, clearly scoped project of about six to twelve weeks, carried out under a non-disclosure agreement, with samples and a measurement protocol provided by the requesting company, and with the possibility of a longer-term joint research project, for example under a European research funding programme, should the initial validation succeed.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Required: an operational ODMR setup for NV-centre characterisation — 532 nm excitation, microwave control around 2.87 GHz, fluorescence detection (confocal or wide-field); ability to measure macroscopic coated plate samples. CW-ODMR is required; Pulsed ODMR (Ramsey / spin-echo) is a plus; temperature- and strain-dependent measurement capability is desirable. Practical: capacity to start within weeks, willingness to work under NDA; samples and measurement protocol will be supplied by the Dutch company.

candidate.description_text: Background Biomethane injected into the natural gas grid must comply with strict gas quality specifications. One of these requirements is that the gas must have the same odor characteristics as natural gas, which is achieved through the addition of an odorant. During biomethane production, Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) can occasionally be present in the gas stream. These compounds may mask the odorant, resulting in reduced odor perception and potentially causing the biomethane to fail grid injection requirements. To prevent this issue, Volatile Organic Compounds are typically removed using activated carbon filtration systems. However, it is often difficult to determine when an activated carbon filter is approaching saturation. As a result, Volatile Organic Compounds breakthrough can occur before filter replacement is initiated. Technical Challenge We are seeking a monitoring solution capable of detecting or predicting the breakthrough of volatile fatty acids in activated carbon filters used in biomethane production facilities. The ideal system should: Continuously or periodically monitor the gas stream downstream of the activated carbon filter. Detect the presence of volatile fatty acids at very low concentrations before they reach levels that can interfere with odor perception. Provide early warning of impending filter saturation or breakthrough. Operate reliably in biomethane production environments. Be suitable for integration into existing gas treatment installations. Expected Outcome The objective is to develop a reliable method for determining the optimal replacement moment of activated carbon filters, thereby preventing Volatile Organic Compounds breakthrough, ensuring compliance with biomethane grid injection specifications, and reducing unnecessary filter replacement costs.

Sensor technologies capable of detecting Volatile Organic Compounds in biomethane streams. Online analytical instruments or monitoring systems. Innovative methods for predicting activated carbon saturation and optimizing filter replacement intervals. Expertise in gas quality monitoring for biomethane and renewable gas applications. Type of Cooperation Sought Commercial agreement with technical assistance Technical cooperation agreement Research and development cooperation Pilot or demonstration projects

candidate.description_text: The company is a major Ukrainian food manufacturer with two factories in Kharkiv and Cherkasy, Ukraine. The manufacturer works in a real production environment where energy continuity, efficiency and resilience are strategically important. The company is now looking for European partners that can offer practical green and clean technologies for an operating food factory. The goal is to reduce energy risks, improve sustainability, and increase autonomy during blackouts and other disruptions. The Ukrainian enterprise is especially interested in solar photovoltaic systems, large battery energy storage systems, smart energy management, industrial heat recovery, and solutions that help reduce greenhouse gas emissions from boiler and thermal processes. The company is also interested in solutions that can capture, reduce or monitor emissions from gas-based production processes, as well as technologies that can recover and reuse heat from waffle cup baking and other thermal operations. The Ukrainian manufacturer is ready to act as a pilot and demonstration site. The company would welcome technical partners that want to test, adapt and validate their solution in a real industrial setting and, where relevant, prepare a joint application for grant funding or other co-financing.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking European partners with practical technologies and engineering expertise in industrial energy efficiency, renewable energy integration and decarbonisation for food manufacturing facilities, interested in pilot projects and grant funding: 1. Solar PV and other renewable / low-carbon energy generation: Technology developers, EPC contractors and integrators of solar PV systems and other renewable or low-carbon on-site energy generation solutions for industrial facilities. The company is interested in an initial pilot or first deployment of approximately 500 kWp–1 MWp of installed solar PV capacity, with possible further expansion up to 2 MWp or more depending on roof/land availability, grid connection conditions and project economics. Relevant solutions may include solar PV, hybrid PV + BESS systems, heat pumps, waste heat utilisation, biogas/biomass-based generation and high-efficiency cogeneration where it provides measurable energy savings and CO₂ reduction. 2. Battery energy storage systems: Suppliers and integrators of modular industrial battery energy storage systems with an initial pilot size of approximately 500 kW–1 MW AC-rated power output and 1–2 MWh usable storage capacity, scalable up to 2 MW / 4 MWh or more. The solution should be suitable for peak shaving, integration with solar PV, backup of critical refrigeration loads, and improved resilience of an operating food production facility with seasonal power demand of up to approximately 1.7 MW. The system should include PCS, BMS, EMS, thermal management, fire safety systems, monitoring software, commissioning support and scalability for future expansion. 3. Industrial waste heat recovery: Companies working with industrial waste heat recovery and thermal storage solutions for food manufacturing facilities. The company is looking for technologies to recover heat from gas-fired wafer cone baking ovens, gas boiler rooms, diesel generators used during blackouts, refrigeration systems, compressors and condensers. The recovered heat could be used for hot water, washing/CIP processes, space heating, preheating, defrosting and other factory needs. Relevant solutions may include flue gas heat recovery, generator exhaust heat recovery, economisers, heat exchangers, industrial heat pumps, thermal storage tanks, smart controls and integration with existing factory utilities. 4. Emissions reduction, flue gas treatment and carbon management: Providers of emissions reduction, flue gas treatment and carbon management solutions for industrial food production facilities. The company is interested in reducing emissions and improving energy efficiency related to gas-fired wafer cone baking ovens, gas boiler rooms, diesel generators used during blackouts and possible future cogeneration systems. Relevant solutions may include flue gas heat recovery, boiler efficiency upgrades, low-NOx burners, exhaust gas treatment where applicable, fuel switching, electrification measures, emissions monitoring, carbon footprint calculation, Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions assessment, and practical decarbonisation roadmaps with measurable reduction targets.
candidate.title: Ukrainian ice cream manufacturer seeks green energy, heat recovery and decarbonisation technologies for pilot deployment and joint grant-based projects

candidate.description_text: The Ukrainian manufacturing SME based in Poltava has practical experience in metalworking, steel structures, roofing and facade systems, woodworking and furniture production. The company operates its own production capacity and plans to expand into a new family of modular metal-and-timber products for veteran and social infrastructure. The planned project will establish a dedicated production and training facility for modular furniture, shelving and storage systems, partitions, workstations, kitchen and sanitary modules, accessibility elements, outdoor furniture and other adaptable solutions. Products are intended to be durable, repairable, easy to disassemble, relocate, reconfigure and reuse. The first practical batch is planned for a veteran centre in Poltava, while the facility will also provide practical training, internships and employment opportunities for Ukrainian veterans. The company is seeking a partner from the Netherlands able to contribute technical know-how in circular design, modular construction, standardised product architecture, design for disassembly, production methodology, quality requirements and knowledge transfer. A key cooperation option is the joint development of a modular frame and connection logic that can be manufactured locally in Ukraine and applied across several product families. The expected result of the international cooperation is a locally manufacturable, standardised and replicable modular product system, supported by technical documentation, production guidance and transfer of know-how to the Ukrainian engineering and production team. The cooperation is intended to support preparation and implementation of a partnership project under the Ukraine Partnership Facility or a comparable reconstruction-oriented cooperation framework.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought Dutch partner should have relevant expertise in one or more of the following areas: - modular steel and/or metal-and-timber systems; - circular product or construction design, including design for disassembly, repair and reuse; - detachable and standardised connection systems; - parametric design and standardisation of product families; - production engineering, manufacturability, assembly methodology and quality control; - preparation of technical documentation, design rules and production standards; - knowledge transfer and practical training for engineering and production teams. Experience in circular construction, modular manufacturing, social infrastructure or reconstruction projects would be an advantage. The partner should be willing to co-develop solutions that can be manufactured by the Ukrainian company rather than only supply finished imported products.
